title: Dependency hardening guide and fallback templates for private deployments
content:
Purpose:
This is a working guide for hardening runtime and control-plane dependencies when upgrading private deployments (VPC and on-prem appliances). It collects the dependency matrix, safe migration patterns, and a set of copy-paste rollback templates we can use during cutovers.

Scope: (what this doc covers)
- Runtime binary and library version bumps (torch/ggml/backends), kernel/driver compatibility notes for on-prem appliances, and required OS/package pins.
- Control plane API surface changes that require client shims or feature gates.
- Terraform module changes that impact resource addresses, provider versions, or state layout.
- Canary/rollout patterns and concrete rollback commands and minimal remediation steps.

Non-goals:
- Deep perf tuning for models (separate perf runbook).
- Customer-facing upgrade scheduling (handled by CS runbooks).

Background/Why we need this:
- Private deployments vary across customer kernels, NICs, and local package versions. A naive runtime or control-plane change can create silent failures (KV cache corruption, model OOMs, or API 500s).
- Historically we saw two classes of incidents: 1) TF state/address changes breaking apply, 2) runtime compatibility causing degraded inference without clear errors. This doc aims to reduce blast radius.

Key concepts / glossary:
- Runtime artifact: the model serving binary + associated libs (eg, inference-engine v2.1.0, kvcache v0.9).
- Control plane API: routes the customer control-plane uses (admin, model-pins, rollout-policy endpoints).
- Shim: a temporary compatibility layer (reverse proxy or API adapter) that translates old requests to new verbs.
- TF adjacency: whether a TF module change requires a state migration or resource recreation (high/medium/low).

Dependency matrix (example, keep small and add rows per release):
- inference-engine: 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 (kernel ABI change) -> risk: high on older kernels.
- kvcache: 0.9 -> 1.0 (on-disk format change, backward-incompatible) -> risk: high unless run with cache-migration tool.
- grpc-proto: 1.3.x -> 1.4.0 (added required field) -> risk: medium, shim possible.
- tf-modules/base: v2024.11 -> v2025.01 (renamed resource address for network attachment) -> TF adjacency: medium, state-move required.

Preconditions checklist (must be green before any rollout window):
- Customer-specific binary compatibility table created and verified for target kernels/drivers. (owner: solutions-eng)
- TF module diffs reviewed with resource address changes explicitly called out. (owner: infra)
- Automated preflight tests pass in a staging appliance that mimics customer config. (owner: QA)
- Snapshot of customer config/state taken and stored: TF state export, runtime snapshots, and monitoring baseline. (owner: SRE)

Phased upgrade plan (recommended):
Phase 0 -- prep and dry-run (week prior):
- Publish change summary with explicit impact and rollback plan to customer contact.
- Create a dedicated canary namespace in customer staging or a dedicated appliance.
- Run full integration preflight (smoke, KV consistency, model-loads, latency p95).
- Run TF plan with replace proposals and simulate state-move locally.

Phase 1 -- isolated canary (2–4 hours window):
- Deploy runtime artifact to canary nodes only.
- Enable verbose tracing, keep 1% traffic to canary (if serving production) and shadow production traffic to canary for 1 hour.
- Run canary-specific test suite (see smoke tests below).
- If any failure: trigger immediate rollback (see templates).

Phase 2 -- controlled ramp (4–8 hours):
- If canary is healthy, increase to 10–25% for 2 hours with closer monitoring.
- Apply TF module changes that are low-adjacency first, then medium. Pause between changes for 30–60 minutes.

Phase 3 -- full cutover (maintenance window):
- Schedule 1–3 hour window depending on adjacency.
- Batch TF state-moves and provider upgrades during a single maintenance transaction if possible.
- Monitor KPIs and be ready to run rollback templates.

Terraform module considerations and concrete notes:
- Always create a preview branch for state moves: include a plan that uses 'terraform state mv' commands in the PR description with exact addresses.
- If a module renames resource addresses, provide a deterministic migration script (example in GH PR). Test the script against a copy of TF state prior to production.
- Pin provider versions in modules to avoid provider-driven diffs during apply. Example: provider.aws = "~> 4.50".
- For customers using remote state backends, coordinate lock acquisition and verification with their platform team. Never run state-moves without a verified snapshot and a documented rollback.

Rollback templates (copyable) -- keep these handy in the incident channel:
- Runtime immediate rollback (k8s):
  - kubectl -n <ns> rollout undo deploy/inference-engine --to-revision=<previous-revision>
  - if pod crashloop, kubectl describe pod <pod> and copy logs to SRE channel before rollback.
- Runtime appliance rollback (bare-metal images):
  - Boot into recovery image, mount /var/lib/inference/snapshots, restore snapshot:<timestamp>
  - Re-run appliance healthcheck: /opt/redwood/bin/healthcheck --full
- KV cache format rollback (if migration failed):
  - Stop inference service
  - Run cache-rollback-tool restore --backup <path> --target-dir /var/lib/kvcache
  - Start service and validate cache checksums
- TF state rollback (resource address mistake):
  - terraform state pull > state-before.json
  - terraform state rm <new.address>
  - terraform state mv <old.address> <new.address>
  - terraform apply (in a dry-run then apply)

Smoke tests (post-change smoke suite):
- API health check: /health returns 200 and all subsystems green.
- Sample inference: run 10 representative prompts across short/long seq lengths and confirm token count, first byte latency, and no 5xxs.
- KV cache sanity: store->retrieve roundtrip for known keys and validate eviction behavior.
- Control-plane API: model-pinning and rollout policy update should succeed and reflect within 5s.
- TF idempotency check: run terraform plan twice; second run must be empty diff.

Monitoring & alert thresholds to watch during ramp:
- Error rate: > 1% 5xxs for > 5m -> pause rollouts.
- Latency p95 increase > 2x baseline for > 10m -> investigate and consider rollback.
- OOM/eviction spikes on nodes -> reduce traffic to affected pool and redeploy.
- TF apply failures > 0 in the batch -> abort and run state diff/rollback.

Customer communication checklist (templated bullet points):
- What we’re changing and why (plain language).
- Expected maintenance window and impact (eg, transient 10-30s per-pod restart).
- Post-upgrade checks we will run and what customers should verify.
- Who to contact and Escalation path (oncall + solutions-eng).

Post-upgrade: validation and cleanups:
- Keep debug logging at INFO level for 24h, then rotate to ERROR once stable.
- Remove shims (if used) only after 72h stable and verification from customers.
- If TF moved state addresses, run 'terraform plan' and commit the final state snapshot to the backup store.
- Schedule a postmortem if any rollback was triggered; capture timeline, decision points, and remediation actions.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Need to add a binary compatibility matrix per-kernel version (ask infra for list of top-10 customer kernels).
- Decide on an official cache-migration tool API contract so it can be backported into appliances.
- Draft short customer-facing FAQ for cache migration scenarios.
- Create a runbook subpage for TF state-move scripts with safe dry-run helpers.

Appendix: quick command references
- TF state export/backup: terraform state pull > state-$(date +%F-%T).json
- TF import example: terraform import module.net.aws_vpc.main vpc-0a1b2c3d
- Appliance healthcheck: /opt/redwood/bin/healthcheck --full --output json

Notes: this is a working draft. I expect infra and QA to add concrete test artifacts (preflight artifact list, sample state files) and add the exact GH PR links for the migration scripts. If you copy from this doc into a PR description, please tag the owners in the checklist above.

Last reviewed: 2025-02-02 by Aisha Patel (in_review)
